question: "Old buildings were built to last — look how many are still standing." What is wrong with this?
options: The badly built ones already fell down
Old buildings are repaired more often
answer: Every era built badly and well. Only the well-built survive to be admired, so any century looks like a golden age from far enough away. The comparison you want is against everything built then, most of which is gone.
move: Every past era looks well made, because the bad parts are not there to see.
trap: Judging a period by what is left of it.
source: Survivorship bias in the built environment
